5	\label{sec:applicability}
6	
7	\looseness=-1 The multi-sample pipeline requires stochastic action diversity across samples. We validate this prerequisite on two VLA architectures: SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} (flow matching, 0.4B) and OpenVLA-OFT~\cite{kim2024openvla} (deterministic $L_1$ regression, 7B).
8	
9	SmolVLA produces meaningfully diverse action samples across all dimensions via its flow-matching generative process. In contrast, OpenVLA-OFT's deterministic $L_1$ regression produces near-identical outputs: mean pairwise $L_2{=}0.00436$ across $K{=}2$ samples, with $97.3$\% of steps below $0.01$. The uncertainty gate never fires, and multi-sample selection is vacuous.
10	
11	This result establishes an architectural boundary: multi-sample inference-time correction is specific to stochastic generative VLAs (flow matching, diffusion). Deterministic VLAs lack the action diversity that selection and correction rely on. The boundary is architectural, not a limitation of our method: any inference-time approach that draws multiple action candidates requires the base policy to produce diverse samples.

13	\section{Cross-VLA Analysis: Model Capability Dependency}
14	\label{sec:cross_vla}

The same K-matched design ($K{=}2$, $\varepsilon{=}0.2$, shared CRM architecture) is used. """
Magnitude sensitivity curve — Spatial only, half-column single panel.
Output: magnitude_curve.pdf
"""

import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import ScalarFormatter

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Times New Roman'],
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 7,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.5,
    'lines.markersize': 5,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.03,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
})

# === LIBERO-Spatial data (seed 42 only) ===
eps_spatial = np.array([0.05, 0.10, 0.30, 1.42])
obs_only_spatial = np.array([35, 35, 36, 35])
perdof_spatial = np.array([31, 35, 26, 0])
argmin_spatial = 34
vla_only_spatial = 30

# === Single panel ===
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(3.3, 1.5))

ax.axvspan(0.05, 0.2, alpha=0.06, color='#6FA8D2', zorder=0)

ax.plot(eps_spatial, obs_only_spatial, 'o-', color='#6FA8D2',
        markerfacecolor='#6FA8D2', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
        label='obs\_only', zorder=5)
ax.plot(eps_spatial, perdof_spatial, '^--', color='#D08888',
        markerfacecolor='#D08888', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
        label='perdof', zorder=5)

ax.axhline(argmin_spatial, color='#555555', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.9,
           label=f'Argmin ({argmin_spatial}%)', zorder=2)
ax.axhline(vla_only_spatial, color='#999999', linestyle='-.', linewidth=0.7,
           label=f'VLA-only ({vla_only_spatial}%)', zorder=2)

ax.annotate('0%', xy=(1.42, 0), xytext=(0.8, 6),
            fontsize=7, color='#D08888', fontweight='bold', ha='center',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#D08888', lw=0.7))

ax.set_xscale('log')
ax.set_xticks(eps_spatial)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(ScalarFormatter())
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
ax.set_xticklabels(['0.05', '0.1', '0.3', r'$\sim$1.42'])
ax.set_xlabel(r'$\varepsilon$')
ax.set_ylabel('SR (%)')
ax.set_ylim(-3, 42)
ax.set_xlim(0.04, 2.0)
ax.legend(loc='lower left', framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='none',
          borderpad=0.3, handlelength=1.5)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='-', alpha=0.15, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

plt.tight_layout()

out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
fig.savefig(os.path.join(out_dir, 'magnitude_curve.pdf'), format='pdf')
fig.savefig(os.path.join(out_dir, 'magnitude_curve.png'), format='png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("Saved: magnitude_curve.pdf, magnitude_curve.png")

"""
Magnitude sensitivity curve — LIBERO-Object (multi-seed), for appendix.
Output: magnitude_curve_object.pdf
"""

import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import ScalarFormatter

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Times New Roman'],
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 8,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.5,
    'lines.markersize': 5,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.03,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
})

# === LIBERO-Object data (Director-locked, 2026-05-18) ===
obs_only_object = {
    0.03: [16],
    0.05: [13, 15, 15, 14],
    0.10: [19, 16, 17, 16, 15, 14],
    0.20: [22, 16, 16, 16, 15, 20, 18],
    0.30: [19, 18, 14, 17, 16],
    1.42: [17, 16, 10],
}

perdof_object = {
    0.03: [14],
    0.05: [14, 9],
    0.10: [11, 11, 8, 13, 12, 11],
    0.20: [11, 9, 10, 12, 9, 11, 7],
    0.30: [4, 5, 5],
    1.42: [0, 0, 0],
}

vla_only_obj_seeds = [12, 12, 10, 11, 13]
argmin_obj_seeds = [12, 17, 13, 12, 10, 10]
vla_only_obj_mean = np.mean(vla_only_obj_seeds)
argmin_obj_mean = np.mean(argmin_obj_seeds)

eps_vals = sorted(obs_only_object.keys())
obs_means = [np.mean(obs_only_object[e]) for e in eps_vals]
obs_stds = [np.std(obs_only_object[e], ddof=1) if len(obs_only_object[e]) > 1 else 0 for e in eps_vals]
obs_ns = [len(obs_only_object[e]) for e in eps_vals]

per_eps = sorted(perdof_object.keys())
per_means = [np.mean(perdof_object[e]) for e in per_eps]
per_stds = [np.std(perdof_object[e], ddof=1) if len(perdof_object[e]) > 1 else 0 for e in per_eps]
per_ns = [len(perdof_object[e]) for e in per_eps]

eps_arr = np.array(eps_vals)
per_arr = np.array(per_eps)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(5.0, 2.5))

ax.axvspan(0.05, 0.2, alpha=0.06, color='#6FA8D2', zorder=0)

ax.plot(eps_arr, obs_means, '-', color='#6FA8D2', linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)
obs_multi_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(obs_ns) if n > 1]
obs_single_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(obs_ns) if n == 1]
if obs_multi_idx:
    ax.errorbar(eps_arr[obs_multi_idx], [obs_means[i] for i in obs_multi_idx],
                yerr=[obs_stds[i] for i in obs_multi_idx], fmt='o', color='#6FA8D2',
                markerfacecolor='#6FA8D2', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
                capsize=3, capthick=0.8, elinewidth=0.8, label='obs\_only', zorder=5)
if obs_single_idx:
    ax.plot(eps_arr[obs_single_idx], [obs_means[i] for i in obs_single_idx], 'D',
            color='#6FA8D2', markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='#6FA8D2',
            markeredgewidth=1.0, markersize=5, zorder=5)

ax.plot(per_arr, per_means, '--', color='#D08888', linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)
per_multi_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(per_ns) if n > 1]
per_single_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(per_ns) if n == 1]
if per_multi_idx:
    ax.errorbar(per_arr[per_multi_idx], [per_means[i] for i in per_multi_idx],
                yerr=[per_stds[i] for i in per_multi_idx], fmt='^', color='#D08888',
                markerfacecolor='#D08888', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
                capsize=3, capthick=0.8, elinewidth=0.8, label='perdof', zorder=5)
if per_single_idx:
    ax.plot(per_arr[per_single_idx], [per_means[i] for i in per_single_idx], 'D',
            color='#D08888', markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='#D08888',
            markeredgewidth=1.0, markersize=5, zorder=5)

ax.axhline(argmin_obj_mean, color='#555555', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.9,
           label=f'Argmin ({argmin_obj_mean:.1f}%)', zorder=2)
ax.axhline(vla_only_obj_mean, color='#999999', linestyle='-.', linewidth=0.7,
           label=f'VLA-only ({vla_only_obj_mean:.1f}%)', zorder=2)

ax.set_xscale('log')
ax.set_xticks(eps_arr)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(ScalarFormatter())
ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
ax.set_xticklabels(['0.03', '0.05', '0.1', '0.2', '0.3', r'$\sim$1.42'])
ax.set_xlabel(r'$\varepsilon$')
ax.set_ylabel('SR (%)')
ax.set_ylim(-2, 28)
ax.set_xlim(0.025, 2.0)
ax.set_title('LIBERO-Object', fontsize=10, pad=3)
ax.legend(loc='upper left', framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='none',
          borderpad=0.3, handlelength=1.5)
ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='-', alpha=0.15, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

plt.tight_layout()

out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
fig.savefig(os.path.join(out_dir, 'magnitude_curve_object.pdf'), format='pdf')
fig.savefig(os.path.join(out_dir, 'magnitude_curve_object.png'), format='png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("Saved: magnitude_curve_object.pdf, magnitude_curve_object.png")

1	\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related_work}
2	
3	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{VLA robustness.} VLAs have progressed from tokenized prediction~\cite{brohan2023rt2,kim2024openvla,ghosh2024octo} to flow matching~\cite{black2024pi0,shukor2025smolvla}, yet lose over 65\,pp under deployment perturbations~\cite{fei2025liberoplus}. Training-time defenses~\cite{srpo2025,robustvla2025,digflow2025} and test-time RL adaptation~\cite{liu2026ttvla} improve robustness but require modifying VLA weights.
4	
5	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{Inference-time correction.} Among frozen-VLA methods, ReconVLA~\cite{chen2026reconvla} quantifies uncertainty without learned correction; SC-VLA~\cite{liu2026scvla} requires RL; VLA-Pilot~\cite{li2025vlapilot} uses evolutionary search at 2.41\,s per step. A2C2~\cite{a2c2_2025}, the closest concurrent work, learns a correction head for temporal staleness but applies it unconditionally. Our pipeline detects \emph{when correction would hurt}, using calibrated gating to suppress correction on confident steps. Residual policy learning~\cite{silver2018residual,johannink2019residual} shares the additive structure; magnitude control is addressed by gating~\cite{jiang2024transic}, clipping~\cite{xiao2026pld}, or decay~\cite{pan2025drc}. Our CRM uses fixed $L_2$ clipping with supervised loss, requiring no RL.
6	
7	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{Selective prediction.} Our $\tau$-gating is an instance of selective prediction~\cite{chow1970optimum,elyaniv2010selective,geifman2017selective}. Unlike SelectiveNet~\cite{geifman2019selectivenet}, we use a pairwise distance threshold with no additional learned components. The $K{=}2$ $L_2$ distance is a minimal ensemble disagreement measure~\cite{lakshminarayanan2017simple}, requiring no architectural changes. Conformal prediction~\cite{angelopoulos2023gentle} has been applied to robotics~\cite{lindemann2023safe,zhao2024conformalized,yao2025cpnav}; our threshold draws on this calibration philosophy without formal coverage guar
…[truncated 423 chars]

1	We show that learned post-hoc correction of frozen flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models is harmful by default, not because the correction module is poor, but because the vast majority of control steps do not need it. On most steps, the VLA already produces confident, low-variance actions; corrections applied here act as noise, degrading performance across all evaluated task suites and model scales. This motivates a shift from improving correction quality to deciding \emph{when to correct at all}. We propose a calibrated gating mechanism that draws two stochastic action samples from the frozen VLA in a single batched forward pass, at zero extra latency, and uses their pairwise distance as a per-step uncertainty proxy. A threshold on this distance gates a lightweight correction module: confident steps pass through unchanged, while only genuinely uncertain steps receive learned residual correction. Across four LIBERO manipulation suites on two VLAs spanning an order of magnitude in scale, selective gating recovers nearly all degradation caused by unconditional correction, with recovery magnitude correlating monotonically with task difficulty. The key finding is that knowing when \emph{not} to correct matters more than the correction itself.
